title: Enforce Circle parent privacy and bound remote QR logo reads
detail: Privileged Circle shell reads now check the owning Space status, visibility and canonical Circles module switch before reading a roster or returning identity. Active private Space viewers retain enabled-module access, while canonical writers/staff retain disabled-module stewardship; legacy unpartitioned Circles retain their existing behavior. Circle autocomplete uses the authenticated session client so parent and Circle RLS filters run before the result limit. Remote QR logo fetches reject redirects and consume a stream with a 512KB retained-byte bound and cancellation, instead of allocating an unlimited arrayBuffer before checking its size. Offline regressions exercise actual shell and route consumers, private-parent denial, writer exceptions, redirect failure, private DNS, streamed bounds and successful image inlining. No live network exploit, database mutation, production behavior or applied-policy verification is claimed. Initial DNS validation is retained; fetch still resolves independently, so DNS pinning/TOCTOU is a residual limitation. Production deployment and database-policy verification remain release gates.

verify.note: Cheap source wiring guard. Separate focused run: seven suites /120 assertions pass, including controlled DNS, fetch, session and database behavior. No actual internal or external endpoints contacted. Local proof only; full release checks remain separate.
